1. Heard Mr. Shiv Vilas Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants, Mr. Shambhavi Nandan, learned
counsel for the opposite party no.2 as well as Mr. D.P. Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

Initially, the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed to quash the entire proceedings of the case including charge sheet dated 02.03.2024, Summoning order dated 24.07.2024, in Case No.33252 of 2024 (State vs. Somai and Others), arising out of Case Crime No.197 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 I.P.C., Police Station- Belipar, District- Gorakhpur as well as stay the further proceedings of the aforesaid case, pending before the Judicial Magistrate-II, District- Gorakhpur.

sentences.text: 3. Today, learned counsel for the applicants has confined his relief to set aside the summoning order dated 24.07.2024.

Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the summoning order dated 24.07.2024 has been passed by the Judicial Magistrate-II, District- Gorakhpur without applying his judicial mind on a printed format and the same is vague, ambiguous and nullity.
He next submits that the perusal of the summoning order indicates that except for directing the office to summon the applicants, absolutely no reasons have been mentioned in support thereof.
He further submits that it is settled law that every orders are to be judged on reasons recorded therein.

He therefore,
submits that summoning order be set aside.

4. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 does not dispute the correctness of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicants and they have no objection if the summoning order is set aside.
5. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the records of the present application.
It is an admitted position that the cognizance order/summoning order dated 24.07.2024 has been passed without application of mind on a printed format.

Such summoning orders passed on a printed proforma have already been set aside by this Court while passing a detail order dated 11th November, 2020 in Application U/S. 482 No.
41617 of 2019 (Vishnu Kumar Gupta & Another Vs. State of U.P. & Another).
6.

entities.text: Vishnu Kumar Gupta & Another Vs. State of U.P. & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, for the reasons recorded in the case of Vishnu Kumar Gupta (Supra), cognizance order/summoning order dated 24.07.2024 is set aside.

The Judicial Magistrate-II, District- Gorakhpur after perusing the entire records shall pass a fresh speaking and reasoned order, in accordance with law, preferably within two months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
7. This Court finds that despite repeated orders of this Court on judicial side as well as administrative side cognizance/summoning orders have been passed on printed proforma.

The Judicial Magistrate-II, District- Gorakhpur is directed to take all precautions so that such orders do not come before this Court otherwise necessary action will taken against the concerned officers as well as concerned District Judge.
8. With the aforesaid directions/observations, this application stands allowed.
9. Office is directed to sent a copy of this order to the Judicial Magistrate-II, District- Gorakhpur within a week.
